description:
Found by s492c member 11 (#2062) on the COMBINED s492b+s492c tree, and it is
the gap the old behaviour was hiding.

t/io/pipe.t row 25 is

    open NIL, '/no_such_process |';
    close NIL;
    my $child = 0;
    eval { local $SIG{ALRM} = sub { die; }; alarm 2; $child = wait; alarm 0; };
    is($child, -1, 'child reaped if piped program cannot be executed');

Under perl the row passes because there is NOTHING LEFT TO REAP: `wait`
returns -1 at once and the alarm never fires.  Under PCL the ALARM FIRES --
which is the proof that `wait` BLOCKED, i.e. some child of an EARLIER test in
the file was still unreaped.  Measured, not inferred: with p-wait's old
blanket guard restored the file reads 20/12 (twice) and with the #2062 fix it
reads 19/13, and the difference is exactly whether the 2-second ALRM handler's
die is swallowed.  In isolation the row's own code answers -1 in 0 seconds
under PCL, identical to perl (scratchpad pipe1.pl), so the leak is upstream in
the file, not in this row.

WHAT TO MEASURE FIRST: run t/io/pipe.t under PCL with a `wait`-loop appended
(or print `getppid`-keyed /proc children) after each of its pipe tests, and
find the first test that leaves a child.  io/pipe.t forks through `open` pipes,
`open2`-style pairs and `fork` directly; the suspects are the failed-exec
child (`/no_such_process |`), the `close` of a pipe whose child already died,
and the socketpair tests.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ROW: an unreaped child is a zombie for the life of
the process, and a program that later calls `wait` gets THAT pid instead of
its own child's -- silently, once.  The row is blessed as failing in
baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv with this task as its cause.
subject: PCL leaves a child UNREAPED in t/io/pipe.t where perl has none -- `wait` blocks and the file's ALRM row fails honestly
